records.title: Silk Road launches
records.summary: US prosecutors later alleged that Ross Ulbricht created Silk Road in approximately January 2011 and operated it as an anonymous online marketplace using Bitcoin.
records.significance: Silk Road became Bitcoin's first globally notorious commercial use case and permanently linked early crypto history with censorship resistance, darknet markets and law enforcement.

sources.title: US DOJ — Ross Ulbricht / Silk Road indictment

records.title: Namecoin launches
records.summary: Namecoin launched as an early Bitcoin-derived blockchain focused on decentralized naming.
records.significance: It was one of the first important altcoins and demonstrated that blockchain could secure namespaces as well as monetary balances.

records.title: Satoshi says he has 'moved on to other things'
records.summary: In his final known email to Mike Hearn, Satoshi wrote that he had moved on to other things and that Bitcoin was in good hands with Gavin and everyone.
records.significance: The creator's departure became one of Bitcoin's central mysteries and a defining decentralization milestone.

sources.title: Satoshi final email to Mike Hearn

records.title: WikiLeaks publicly accepts Bitcoin donations
records.summary: WikiLeaks announced that it was accepting anonymous Bitcoin donations after conventional payment channels had been restricted.
records.significance: The episode became one of the clearest early demonstrations of Bitcoin's censorship-resistant payment narrative.

sources.title: Forbes — WikiLeaks asks for Bitcoin donations

records.title: Gavin Andresen presents Bitcoin at a CIA event
records.summary: Gavin Andresen later wrote that he had given a Bitcoin presentation at a CIA event the previous Tuesday.
records.significance: The episode captured early tension between Bitcoin's cypherpunk roots and growing government interest.

sources.title: BitcoinTalk — Gavin Andresen CIA talk follow-up

records.title: Mt. Gox security breach triggers dramatic flash crash
records.summary: A compromised Mt. Gox account was used to dump Bitcoin, driving the quoted price from roughly $17 to pennies before trading was halted and transactions were later rolled back.
records.significance: The incident was Bitcoin's first globally visible exchange-security crisis and exposed the systemic risk of centralized exchange concentration.

sources.title: WIRED — Bitcoin Prices Plummet on Hacked Exchange
BitMEX Research — June 2011 Bitcoin Flash Crash

records.title: BitInstant launches as an early fiat on-ramp
records.summary: BitInstant was announced as a service designed to move funds rapidly into Bitcoin exchanges.
records.significance: It became part of the first generation of infrastructure connecting conventional money to Bitcoin.

records.title: Casascius physical bitcoins appear
records.summary: Mike Caldwell began producing funded physical Bitcoin coins with private keys protected beneath tamper-evident holograms.
records.significance: Casascius coins turned an intangible digital asset into a physical bearer collectible and became an icon of early Bitcoin culture.

records.title: Litecoin launches
records.summary: Charlie Lee announced Litecoin on 9 October 2011; its genesis block was mined shortly afterward and the planned public launch was 13 October.
records.significance: Litecoin became the longest-lived major early Bitcoin-derived altcoin and popularized Scrypt, faster blocks and the 'digital silver' narrative.

records.title: BTC-e launches
records.summary: US prosecutors later described BTC-e as a cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2011.
records.significance: BTC-e became a major early trading venue and later one of the most important crypto exchanges in international money-laundering enforcement.

sources.title: US DOJ — BTC-e and Alexander Vinnik indictment
